newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBs seen having an upward bias.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBs seen having an upward bias.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to edge higher on Monday, but the upside is seen capped near 124.50, traders said.

"I think JGBs, for the most part, will be stuck in range trade. But in terms of direction, there is a bigger chance that it will try for the upside than the downside," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
The market will focus on whether Tokyo share prices manage to stay above the key 20,000 point level on Monday after a sharp fall in U.S. share prices on Friday, traders said.

"JGBs will be supported if Tokyo share prices break below the 20,000 point level following the sharp fall in the Dow Jones industrial average on Friday," a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.
In New York on Friday, the key Dow Jones industrial average fell 138.88 points, or 1.89 percent, to end at 7,194.67.
If Tokyo share prices begin consolidating at above the 20,000 point level, however, this will cap the upside of JGBs, the first trader said.
Moves in the dollar/yen exchange rate may also become a factor for JGBs today, the second trader said.

If Japan's customs-cleared trade statistics for April due at 2350 GMT show a sharp rise in Japan's trade surplus, it may lead to buying of the yen against the dollar and provide support to JGBs, the second trader said.
The June's rise in London on Friday was probably due to short-covering ahead of the weekend, the first trader said.
The June ended at 124.26 on LIFFE on Friday, up from Friday's Tokyo close of 123.98.
JGBs will likely have an upward bias on Monday, as fears of an imminent rise in Japanese interest rates have subsided, at least for now, the first trader said.
